scope: Social Sciences only. Two disjoint seven-day windows. Each ranking collected its sources and used the selected parent history. Eligible runs reused exact classification and group-review decisions from the same main-branch workflow. Each parent retained its own topic history and embeddings and ran scoring and synthesis independently.
additional_comparison_reason: After both November 5 source requests failed, the archived previous-day lineage was reranked from its previously complete November 5 snapshot. A separate fixed-input check reapplied a single decision set to both original complete snapshots and stopped at ranking, before synthesis.

fixed_input_november_5.source: Two previously complete independently collected November 5 stores. Each preserved its paper records, prior topics and vectors. All classifications and group decisions came from the same retained artifact. The production code recomputed the ranking and stopped before synthesis. Any missing embeddings were calculated locally with the installed SPECTER2 model. No new model-service requests or source downloads.

artifact_selection.observed_error: The original selection sorted numeric file IDs. The first November 12 run restored an older November 5 snapshot. The second November 12 run also missed the first November 12 decisions. The summaries and classifications in these independently assessed versions differed.
artifact_selection.rule: Order by creation time. Reconcile earlier unmarked snapshots using the first retained validated receipt per request, then retain a manifest. The next run can restore one cumulative snapshot.
artifact_selection.verification: Compared the SHA-256 of every inherited classification and review against the archived source runs. A conflict means two different versions of a decision for the same request, including wording-only differences.

fixed_input_november_12.source: Two previously complete independently collected stores for the same date. Each preserved its paper records, prior topics and vectors. Both contexts use the same validated classifications and group decisions. Any classification still unavailable in the selected edition is explicitly held unavailable in both contexts. The production code recomputed the ranking and stopped before synthesis. Any missing embeddings were calculated locally with the installed SPECTER2 model. No new model-service requests or source downloads.

source_checks.method: Compare arXiv identifiers, titles and abstracts with two adjacent, previously successful seven-day collections per date. Filter on original publication date. The earlier windows reconstruct November 5 and the later two reconstruct November 12. This is a retrospective completeness check. The direct API recheck is reported separately.

curriculum_frameworks.judgement: The three papers design methods for integrating digital tools into professional curricula. The Kenyan illustration, the health-professions simulation model and the Malaysian building-information-modelling framework each call for validation. The original articles support the stated six stages, seven propositions and 78-study evidence base respectively.

student_technology_and_civic_trust.judgement: Two Ghanaian samples concern intentions to use educational tools. The third study examines trust in AI and its reported use in civic decisions across Egypt, Kuwait and the UAE. It has a different population and outcome. The archive synthesis distinguishes them. The previous-day headline extends an adoption outcome across the entire group. Its detailed paragraph and the scoped reader note identify the actual outcomes.

student_technology_acceptance.judgement: University students reported intentions to use learning technologies across all three studies. The papers support the stated survey samples of 238, 596 and 294, the interviews in Egypt and the directions of the reported paths. The measured outcomes concern acceptance and reported use, with a self-rated learning experience in the meme study. The other initial headline describes the surveys correctly, but its synthesis says the meme-learning country was unstated. The published methods identify an Indian women’s college and convenience recruitment.

double_machine_learning.judgement: All three papers study conditions for valid inference using double or debiased machine learning. The papers distinguish weak instruments, latent panel confounding and misspecified moments. Section 6 of the GMM paper confirms the Monte Carlo study. The panel paper attaches the minimum-wage association to its identifying assumptions.

classroom_processes.judgement: The Swiss study measured children’s perceived social inclusion, the Kosovo survey related teaching practices to reported socio-emotional competence, and the Chinese quasi-experiment tested changes in competence over time. These three studies share a classroom setting, with different exposures and outcomes. The first run describes each design and states the null and subgroup results separately. The Chinese paper tested whether rates differed by initial competence. The first version placed its null result immediately after the comparison of programmes without naming the tested baseline contrast. The reader note supplies it. The reconciled alternative still leaves the null contrast implicit in the synthesis. Its reader note names the baseline groups.

digital_media_and_conflict.judgement: The authors describe journalism in Mali, political intimidation in Burkina Faso and diaspora political discourse relating to Ethiopia. These are separate communication practices and research questions. The summary describes each qualitative study in its setting.

professional_ai_judgement.judgement: All three examine the ability to evaluate AI outputs in professional education or work. The employer research collected primary data, while the other two propose frameworks. The original articles support the sampling and validation distinctions.

representative_issues.selection: For November 5 use the edition with the complete previous-day lineage, successful live source collection and a checked reader note. For November 12 use the first reconciled edition. Both English issues were verified against their stored rankings and referenced evidence.
mismatched_outcomes: Educational adoption intentions alongside civic trust on November 5.
Social inclusion alongside socio-emotional competence on November 12.

cost.method: Each model ledger less the selected parent ledger. Verified English audit jobs made no model calls. Reused decisions and freshly synthesized prose have different costs.
cost.monthly_budget: Decide after measured field pilots and live-date operating costs.

limitations: The scientific accuracy of the first decision requires separate editorial review. A change to a prompt or source, or the loss of every retained copy, requires fresh decisions.
Different prior published topics can legitimately change continuity labels and the five-percent previous-day score adjustment. Synthesized descriptions can differ across parent stores.
Editorial judgements compare the as-written entries with the cited articles. The high- and low-ranked samples count repeated papers once. These case judgements have one reviewer.
ArXiv freshness, editorial accuracy and 14 live dates remain publication criteria.
